chunk_findings.detail: The reason string blames the wrong setting. The ternary is taken whenever `cfg.dedupe.on_match == "off"` **or** `rec.kind not in cfg.dedupe.kinds`, but it always prints the same tail: `"the check is off ([dedupe].on_match = off)"`. Concretely, with `[dedupe] on_match = "ask"` (the new shipped default) and `kinds = ["incident"]`, running `... add --check` on an `"issue"` record produces `no existing record reads like this: the check is off ([dedupe].on_match = off)`. `on_match` is `"ask"`, so a user (or the MCP caller) chasing why `--check` found nothing is pointed at a setting that is not the cause; the real cause is that the record's kind is excluded from `dedupe.kinds`. The two conditions should produce distinct text.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py — `_dry_run`, the `why` ternary

chunk_findings.detail: When the index cannot be read, `_assess` returns an empty `shown` plus a non-empty `unavailable`, and `_dry_run` falls into the `if not shown:` branch with `why = unavailable`, returning `O.nothing(rec.event_kind, f"no existing record reads like this: {why}", ...)`. So during an index outage `--check` asserts the negative "no existing record reads like this" and exits 2 (the "none reads like it" code), even though by the documented contract for this case the check *did not run* and the add would go ahead. `dedupe_unavailable` is present in the payload so a JSON/MCP consumer can tell, but anything gating on the exit code (e.g. `add --check ... && add ...`) is told "definitely no duplicate" for a result that is actually unknown.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py — `_dry_run`, the `not shown` branch with `unavailable`

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture hard-codes the dedupe mode for every test body: it does `monkeypatch.setenv("DDFLOW_DEDUPE_ON_MATCH", "off")` to seed, then `monkeypatch.setenv("DDFLOW_DEDUPE_ON_MATCH", "ask")` before returning, so all refusal / check_only assertions are driven by the environment variable rather than by the shipped `[dedupe].on_match` default. The stated intent of this change includes "flip the shipped `[dedupe].on_match` default back to `ask`", but no test in this file exercises that default. Concretely: edit the default written by `init` (or the fall-back used when the key is absent) back to `off`/`never` while leaving this diff as-is, and every one of `test_a_refused_add_leads_with_the_candidates_and_the_options`, `test_relation_extends_answers_the_refusal`, `test_check_only_lists_candidates_and_writes_nothing`, etc. still passes, because `make()` re-enables `ask` via `setenv` immediately after `init`. The exact behavior the change is supposed to restore is therefore not covered by this file — a regression of the shipped default would slip through. (If a separate config-level test elsewhere in the change asserts the default, this finding is moot; within part 11 there is none.)
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_add_dedupe_mcp.py:67-70 (the `filed_as` fixture)

chunk_findings.detail: The documented `--check` contract makes "no candidates" exit 2, which is the same code argparse uses for a command-line error (the same paragraph relies on that: "`--new`, `--extends ID`, `--duplicate-of ID`, `--related ID` (at most one; argparse refuses two)"). Given `ddflow task add "x" --check` with no candidates above `show_floor`, the process exits 2 with no candidates; given `ddflow task add "x" --check --new --extends B1`, argparse rejects the combination and the process also exits 2 (usage message on stderr, nothing on stdout). A wrapper/agent that branches on the exit status (the stated use case is scripts and agents, since `--check` is the documented pre-flight) cannot tell "there is nothing similar, go ahead and file" from "your invocation was malformed" — and an invocation that treats 2 as "no candidates, safe to file" will silently proceed after a rejected flag combination. Exit 2 should be reserved for usage errors, or the no-candidate case should use a distinguishable code/output (the JSON branch does expose this, but the plain `--check` path documented here does not).
chunk_findings.title: README.md:1770 (`--check` bullet)

chunk_findings.detail: The diagnostic produced when no candidates are found misstates the cause whenever the reason is the kind filter rather than `on_match`. The branch condition is `cfg.dedupe.on_match == "off" or rec.kind not in cfg.dedupe.kinds`, but the message attached to both arms is the literal string `"the check is off ([dedupe].on_match = off)"`. Concretely, with the new default `[dedupe] on_match = "ask"` and `kinds = ["bug"]`, running `--check` (or MCP `check_only`) for a `note` record skips the search because `"note"` is not in `kinds`, `shown` is empty, and the refusal reads `no existing record reads like this: the check is off ([dedupe].on_match = off)`. The user is told their `on_match` setting is `off` when it is in fact `ask` and the real cause is that the record's kind is not enabled for dedupe, sending them to change the wrong config key. The `rec.kind not in cfg.dedupe.kinds` arm needs its own wording (e.g. naming `[dedupe].kinds`), or the parenthetical must be dropped/reworded so it does not assert a value that is false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py:_dry_run (`why = unavailable or (...)`)

chunk_findings.detail: `commands()` builds each suggested command as `"ddflow " + shlex.join(argv)` with the answer flag appended at the very end. When the original invocation used the `--` end-of-options separator — which is required whenever the free-text title begins with `-` or contains something argparse reads as an option, e.g. `ddflow task add -- "-retry storm"` or `ddflow task add -- "explain the --verbose flag"` — `shlex.join` preserves the literal `--`, and the result is `ddflow task add -- '-retry storm' --new`. Because argparse stops option parsing at `--`, the appended `--new` is consumed as positional text rather than the flag: the add either errors on an unexpected positional or files a brand-new record whose text is `-retry storm --new`. Either way the suggested command does not answer the refusal it was generated for, so the "copy-paste commands" the non-terminal exit-3 refusal advertises are wrong for any invocation that needed `--`. The flag needs to be inserted before the `--` (or the separator dropped) rather than appended to the raw `argv`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/dedupe_flags.py:commands

chunk_findings.detail: The diff flips the shipped default of `[dedupe].on_match` to `"ask"`, and the rewritten `test_shipped_default_withholds_near_duplicates` confirms the new import behavior: with the env override removed, a corpus containing a near-duplicate pair leaves `len(plan.duplicates) == 1` and only `1` record starting with `LS-` — i.e. `ddflow import` now *withholds* the near-duplicate record. But the change only adds answer surfaces (`--new`/`--extends`/`--duplicate-of`/`--related`/`--check`, the terminal prompt, the non-terminal exit‑3 refusal, MCP `relation`/`check_only`) to the **add** commands/add tools; nothing is added to the import command or its tool (the `mcp_parity` overrides even single out `ddflow_import --verify` as the only import-related exemption). So under the shipped default an import that trips the check loses the near-duplicate record, and the import surface offers no flag, prompt, or MCP argument to bring it in — the exact "ask refused with no way through" situation that motivated keeping the default at `"warn"` (the hotfix this change reverts) now reappears for `import`. The updated test only asserts the record is withheld; it never attempts to answer the refusal for the import path, so it cannot catch this regression.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_import_dedupe.py::test_shipped_default_withholds_near_duplicates

chunk_findings.detail: `parse_reply` guards the positional-number branch with `ref.isdigit()` and then calls `int(ref)` to index `rows`. For Python strings, `str.isdigit()` is true for characters with the Unicode "digit" property that `int()` rejects — the superscripts `¹²³` are the common case. If a person answering the interactive menu types, e.g., `e ²` (letter, space, SUPERSCRIPT TWO), `head` becomes `"e"`, `ref` becomes `"²"`, `"²".isdigit()` is `True`, and `int("²")` raises `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '²'`. Nothing in `ask` catches this — the loop only catches `EOFError` — so the whole command dies with a traceback instead of re-printing `Not understood. One of: ...` and re-prompting. The intended "not understood" path is only taken for refs where `isdigit()` is false (or where `isdigit()` is true but the comparison succeeds); a `ref.isdecimal()`/`try: int(...)` guard (or catching `ValueError` in `ask`) would route these inputs to the retry branch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/dedupe_flags.py:parse_reply

chunk_findings.detail:
The guard only clears the response projection when `out.data` carries `extended` or `check_only`:

```python
if not as_text and (out.data.get("extended") or out.data.get("check_only")):
    payload_key = ""
```

But the case the change is written for — a plain add that the dedupe check *refuses* as a possible duplicate — carries neither key. A refusal happens precisely when the caller did **not** pass `check_only` (the value the guard reads is the user-supplied `check_only`, echoed back) and nothing was extended (`extended` is only set once a record was actually appended to). The refusal instead carries `candidates`/`would_ask`/`options`, which is exactly what the tool schemas promise the client receives so it can retry with `relation=...`.

So for input like an MCP call to `ddflow_task_add` with a task body that duplicates an existing open task and `relation`/`check_only` omitted, the refusal data is built, this guard evaluates false, `payload_key` keeps the tool's usual projection (`"payload": ("id",)` / `("id", "line", ...)`), and the projection filters `candidates`/`options`/`would_ask` out of the structured response — the client sees `{"id": null}` (or a dict of nulls) rather than the candidate list the refusal is supposed to hand it. That contradicts the stated non-terminal refusal ("listing candidates and copy-paste commands") and leaves the model with no `ID` to pass to `extends:`/`duplicate_of:`/`related:` on the retry, defeating the `relation` plumbing added in this same change. The same failure applies to any dry run whose result is keyed `candidates`/`would_ask` rather than literally `check_only`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:2733 (the new `payload_key` guard)

chunk_findings.detail: `_dry_run` is reached before the `if rec.kind and kind_of(st, rec.rid) == rec.kind: return Checked()` shortcut, so for a rec whose rid+kind already exist in the index it reports `would_ask: true` (and candidates) even though the identical add without `--check` returns `Checked()` at that shortcut and is never refused — e.g. re-adding `--id D1 --kind decision` with slightly edited text after D1 exists returns `would_ask: true` from `--check` but succeeds silently when run without it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py:308 (`if answer.check_only:` / `_dry_run`)

chunk_findings.detail: The dedupe answer (the relation the user selected: `--new` / `--extends <id>` / `--duplicate-of <id>` / `--related <id>`) is delivered to the API differently in the three otherwise-identical edits. `cmd_memory` passes it as a call argument to the add function (`A.memory_add(..., answer=answer, agent=...)`), which is the only place a relation can go for a memory add, and thus documents the API contract: the add functions take the relation as a parameter. `cmd_lesson` instead constructs `A.LessonDraft(..., answer=answer)` and calls `A.lesson_add(c.repo, draft, agent=...)`, and `cmd_research` constructs `A.Finding(..., answer=answer)` and calls `A.research_add(c.repo, finding, agent=...)`. Neither add function therefore ever receives the `answer`, so the API's relation handling (the same handling that is exercised for memory) is bypassed for lessons and research. Concretely, running `ddflow lesson add --title T --rule R --extends L1` resolves `answer` in `D.run`, builds the draft, and invokes `lesson_add` with no relation argument; if `LessonDraft`/`Finding` have no `answer` field this raises `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'answer'` before the add runs, and if they do, the relation is silently stored as content and never recorded as a dedupe relation, so the candidate the user chose is not linked. The relation belongs on the add call (as in the memory branch), not on the content dataclass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/knowledge.py: cmd_lesson / cmd_research

chunk_findings.detail: `str.isdigit()` returns True for "compatibility" digit characters such as the superscripts `²`/`³`/`⁴` and the subscripts `₂`/`₃`, but `int()` only accepts decimal digits, so the two calls are not interchangeable. Given the reply `e ²` (or `r ³`, `d ⁴`, …), `ask()` lowercases and splits it, `ref` becomes `"²"`, `ref.isdigit()` is True, and `int(ref)` raises `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '²'`. That exception is not caught anywhere in `ask()` (only `EOFError` is), so it propagates out of `run()` and the CLI dies with a traceback instead of printing `Not understood. One of: [n]ew / ...` and re-prompting. The same crash occurs for any input whose final token is a non-decimal Unicode digit. Note `Answer`'s `id`-based fallback below this line is not reached because the exception is raised before it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/dedupe_flags.py:parse_reply (`if ref.isdigit() and 1 <= int(ref) <= len(rows):`)

chunk_findings.detail: The override that clears `payload_key` for extended/check-only add results is guarded by `not as_text`, but the text branch directly below consumes the same `payload_key` when it calls `out.body(payload_key)`. The comment on these added lines says the tool's usual `{"id": ...}` projection "would drop" the check answer, yet the guard leaves that projection in place for every `as_text=True` call. Concrete failure: a client calls `ddflow_task_add` with `{"...": ..., "check_only": true, "as_text": true}`; `_answer` produces `Answer(..., check_only=True)`, the API returns the duplicate-check result, the guard is skipped because `as_text` is true, `payload_key` remains the tool's `("id",)` payload, and `out.body(("id",))` renders only the id projection — the `candidates`/`would_ask` data that the `check_only` property description (added in the same diff) promises is silently missing. The same truncation hits `relation: "extends:ID"` responses (`extended`) in text mode, whereas the identical call without `as_text` returns the full payload. The fix must either drop the `not as_text` guard or render the special result without the id projection in the text branch as well.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:2734 (the `if not as_text and (out.data.get("extended") or out.data.get("check_only")): payload_key = ""` override)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:2734 (the `if not as_text and (out.data.get("extended") or out.data.get("check_only")): payload_key = ""` override)

chunk_findings.detail: The new test module imports `pty` unconditionally at module scope. On Windows, `pty` is not part of the standard library, so `import pty` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` during test collection. Because the import is at the top of the file, the whole module fails to collect — including the non-terminal tests such as `test_without_a_terminal_a_duplicate_is_refused_with_the_commands_that_answer_it`, which do not need a pseudo-terminal at all. The same module also uses `select.select` on a pty master fd, which is Unix-only. The terminal tests should be guarded with `pytest.importorskip("pty")` or marked/skipped on non-POSIX platforms so the rest of the suite can still run.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_add_dedupe_cli.py:7

chunk_findings.detail: The shipped-default flip to `ask` is only answerable on the seven add commands (CLI `--new/--extends/--duplicate-of/--related`, terminal prompt, MCP `relation`/`check_only`). The parity exclusions added in this diff are exactly the seven add tools (`ddflow_phase_add`, `ddflow_task_add`, `ddflow_bug_found`, `ddflow_lesson_add`, `ddflow_decision_add`, `ddflow_research_add`, `ddflow_memory_add`) — `ddflow_import` gets none of these flags (its only entry is the pre-existing `--verify`). With the default now `ask`, the test itself demonstrates that the same “refused with no way through” situation B-dedupe-default-warn was created for now applies to the import surface: given the `_corpus(repo)` fixture (two lessons, one a near-duplicate) and `DDFLOW_DEDUPE_ON_MATCH` unset, `ddflow import` keeps only 1 lesson and withholds the other, while the only way to include it is a global config/env override or a manual re-add. The assertion was changed from `== 2` to `== 1`, so the diff locks in the regression rather than catching it; a batch import in a non-interactive context (CI) now silently loses records that the user asked to import.

chunk_findings.detail: `_dry_run` builds `data` — and therefore evaluates `found.action`, and `exact.id`/`exact.kind` — *before* it tests `if unavailable:`. `_assess` reports "the check did not run" by returning an absent `found` together with the `unavailable` message; that is exactly the contract the enclosing `check_add` docstring relies on and states in this diff: "Never raises for an index that cannot be read: the add goes ahead, and ``unavailable`` says the check did not run." The pre-existing add path only touches `found` after that condition is handled. Consequently, `ddflow note add --check ...` (or any MCP `check_only=True` call) against an unreadable dedupe index — corrupt index file, unreadable permissions, I/O error — raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'action'` instead of returning the intended `O.failed(..., "the duplicate check could not run: ...")` outcome, i.e. the new check path violates `check_add`'s documented never-raises behaviour and the user gets a traceback rather than the "check could not run / not a clean bill" refusal. Note the author already hedged the sibling access with `getattr(found, "identical", None)`, which is what makes the bare `found.action` at this point the defect rather than a sentinel-style design; the fix is to move the `if unavailable:` test above the `data` computation (or read `getattr(found, "action", None)`).
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py:_dry_run (`merged = found.action == "ask" and exact is not None ...`)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py:_dry_run (`merged = found.action == "ask" and exact is not None ...`)

chunk_findings.detail: The guard that disables the add tools' payload projection tests `out.data.get("check_only")`, but the duplicate-check result is documented — in the very `DEDUPE_PROPERTIES` block added by this diff — as returning `candidates` and `would_ask`, not `check_only`. `check_only` is a *request* field; `would_ask` is the *response* field. Concretely: a first MCP call such as `ddflow_task_add` with no `relation` is refused because a possible duplicate exists; the api result is `{"candidates": [...], "would_ask": true, ...}`. `out.data.get("extended")` is `None` and `out.data.get("check_only")` is falsy (the caller never set it, and even an echoed `check_only: false` is falsy), so `payload_key` is not cleared and the tool applies its normal projection (`("id", ...)`). The result is that `candidates` is dropped — the model never sees the records it is supposed to answer with `relation: extends:ID`, which defeats the whole point of the change — and because the refusal payload has no `id`, the projection either yields a useless `{}` or raises `KeyError` depending on how it is applied. The same applies to a `check_only` dry run whose result carries `would_ask`/`candidates`: only a literal `check_only` key in the response (which the docstring does not list) would make the guard fire. The condition should key off the response's own check indicator (`would_ask`, or the presence of `candidates`), not off the request's `check_only`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:~2734 (`payload_key` override guard / `_answer`)
